articles.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Review
articles.summary: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 review: Welcome back to Night City, but beware the corpos.
body: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners felt like a revelation. Like Castlevania and Arcane before it, the series delivered a stunning video game adaptation that told an original story with memorable characters rather than trying to forcefully redo the game’s storyline, all while still very much feeling like a part of its source material’s world. Add in a phenomenal soundtrack and Hiroyuki Imaishi’s striking visual flare, and you have one of the best sci-fi animé series of all time.

Now we’re back in Night City for a new standalone sequel in the larger Cyberpunk universe, though Edgerunners 2 does tie into the story of David Martinez from the first 10-episode series in key ways while also connecting to the main story of Cyberpunk 2077. No, you don’t need to have experienced either to enjoy this new story, but it does pay off to know more about the world of Night City.
points: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 review: Welcome back to Night City, but beware the corpos.

articles.title: 9 Years Later, The Simpsons' Controversial Character Officially Returns
articles.summary: In January 2020, Hank Azaria stepped down from voicing one of the most iconic characters on The Simpsons, Kwik-E-Mart owner Apu Nahasapeemapetilon. The actor and the show's writers agreed that the portrayal of Apu was charged with racial stereotypes, and they apologized while the character and his…
body: The Apu controversy began in 2017 with Indian American comedian Hari Kondabolu's documentary The Problem With Apu, which argued that the character's stereotypical portrayal had been deeply damaging to people of South Asian heritage, to the point that "Apu" began being used as a racial slur. Azaria, who is white, stated that characters of color should be voiced by actors from those communities, so he decided to step down from his role. Meanwhile, Apu became a background character, who made sporadic appearances but never uttered a single word, while the show decided what to do with him.

articles.title: Players on Steam so far seem delighted with Modern Warfare 4's campaign, making it one of the most well-received Call of Dutys in recent history
articles.summary: It may be hard to believe, given all the Call of Duty: Modern 4 pre-launch community drama and the beta's lower-than-expected numbers on PC, but the final game may have turned things around - so far, at least.
body: On Steam, Infinity Ward 's final chapter in the Modern Warfare sub-series currently has a Very Positive (92 percent) rating based on over 3,100 user reviews. Modern Warfare 4's campaign early access went live Friday, and the review rating has been improving steadily as players have experienced more of the campaign's missions. Many have likely finished it by now; the campaign is a little over six-hours in length, after all.

Gaining access to the campaign on Friday required pre-ordering any of the game's editions digitally. Modern Warfare 4's official release isn't until 23rd October, which makes it hard to determine the current number of players, because SteamDB, our source for this data, can't reveal numbers without its tracking bot having a copy of the game.

Setting aside player numbers, the sentiment around Modern Warfare 4 is considerably more positive at the outset compared to last year's Black Ops 7, currently sitting at Mostly Negative (37 percent). While review ratings change over time with each major update, Modern Warfare 4 is currently the highest-rated Call of Duty in over a decade.

articles.title: Tom Cruise's 10/10 War Action Epic Is About to Say Goodbye to HBO Max
articles.summary: Tom Cruise has built a career out of playing larger-than-life characters, but some of his best performances are when he delves into the more vulnerable people beneath the movie-star bravado.
body: The historical backdrop also gives those personal struggles an even greater sense of tragedy. More a fantasy epic than historical retelling, The Last Samurai draws inspiration from the Satsuma Rebellion of 1877, when former samurai led by Saigō Takamori rose against Japan’s rapidly modernizing Meiji government. Katsumoto is loosely based on Saigō, though the film takes considerable liberties with the historical record. Algren, meanwhile, shares some similarities with Jules Brunet, a French military officer who refused orders to leave Japan and fought alongside forces loyal to the shogunate during the Boshin War of 1868-1869, including the short-lived Ezo Republic on Hokkaido.

The film effectively blends these separate historical episodes into a single narrative. The real Satsuma Rebellion was also more complicated than a battle between traditional warriors and modern technology, not least because Saigō’s forces used rifles and artillery themselves. Nevertheless, the film captures the upheaval of an era in which Japan was redefining its national identity, raising difficult questions about what progress demands and what a society risks losing in the process.
points: Tom Cruise has built a career out of playing larger-than-life characters, but some of his best performances are when he delves into the more vulnerable people beneath the movie-star bravado.

articles.title: Netflix's Sci-Fi Cyberpunk Sleeper Hit Becomes a True Masterpiece in Stellar New Season
articles.summary: Across 10 episodes, director Kai Ikarashi and the teams at CD Projekt Red and Studio Trigger deliver another spectacular collision of corporate cruelty, dangerous technology, and people pushing themselves past their limits. The ingredients are familiar, sometimes a little too much.
body: Night City makes it easy to confuse becoming a legend with having a life worth living. Mercenaries replace their flesh with increasingly powerful chrome, take gigs they have no business surviving, and hope somebody remembers their name after it all inevitably goes to hell. The first season of Netflix's Cyberpunk: Edgerunners made a devastating romance out of that bargain. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, which continues the anthology series on Oct. 20, finds something far more hopeful in the same brutal world.

Edgerunners 2 initially threatens to repeat its predecessor. It opens with a heavily augmented man succumbing to cyberpsychosis after a gig goes south. He goes on a grisly killing spree. Another rampage? Another warning about how too much chrome is always a bad idea? This time, the man at the center of the carnage has a life to navigate afterward. Once a celebrated edgerunner known as King, Weak Kingsley (Clancy Brown) emerges as a shell of his former self, hulking arms replaced by frail robot limbs that make C-3PO look buff. Following a burnout like this who lived rather than got obliterated by Militech somehow gives a familiar setup a compelling new direction.

articles.title: Don Bradman Cricket Jr Announced for PC and Consoles
articles.summary: With Cricket 26 developer Big Ant Studios holding somewhat of a monopoly on the cricket videogame genre for more than a decade, fans of the world's second most popular sport have been crying out for some competition within the genre.
body: In comparison, Don Bradman Cricket Jr is arriving eight years late and minus any official team or player licenses, beyond the inclusion of Australia's greatest ever batsman himself as an unlockable character. By completing a specific in-game challenge, players will apparently be able to drop the Don directly into the otherwise entirely generic Australian team, as well as gain access to a bonus minigame that recreates his famous knocking-a-golf-ball-into-a-water-tank-using-a-stump-fo-a-bat training exercise.

Elsewhere, Don Bradman Cricket Jr seems to be offering a fairly basic feature set, with unlicensed tournaments to play and a challenge mode to test your skills with, alongside split-screen support for two players. Not much is known about the actual gameplay, but the developers are promising that the experience of batting will ensure that "no two shots are ever truly the same." This despite the announcement trailer above seeming to show multiple versions of the same pull through mid-wicket.

articles.title: Jesse Eisenberg Says He 'Couldn't Get Movie Studio Parts' After Winning His Batman v. Superman Razzie
articles.summary: Jesse Eisenberg says he "couldn't get into studio movie parts" because he won a Worst Supporting Actor Razzie for playing Lex Luthor in Batman v. Superman. The Social Network star elaborated on what has become one of his most divisive roles when speaking at the BFI London Film Festival (via Variety…
body: "Listen, a lot of it just came from fear," he said when describing his shift away from studio roles. "I couldn’t get into movie studio parts anymore because I had won a Raspberry Award from [being in the] Batman movie … and I saw the trajectory."

Although the polarizing Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice does have its fair share of fans, Eisenberg's more eccentric performance as the Superman villain has remained one of its most controversial elements in the decade since its premiere. His acting was so…memorable that he walked away from the part with a Razzie for Worst Supporting Actor.

Winning at the Golden Raspberry Awards, which recognize the worst components in movies each year, isn't usually treated as an honor. No one wants to be told they are the "worst" at anything, and having that Razzie label attached to your name can sometimes even secure a person's place in the hall of filmmaking infamy.

articles.title: 31 Years Later, Calvin and Hobbes' Scariest Comic Is Still a Controversial Classic
articles.summary: On a Halloween reread of Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes, one of its more remarkable qualities is that it usually doesn't bother with that. There are a few seasonal strips and arcs scattered across its nine-year run, sure, and Calvin's struggle with staying good before Christmas is an annual…
body: Daily newspaper comics usually make a point of being seasonal. It's a rare gag-a-day strip that doesn't make sure to touch upon all the major holidays, particularly Valentine's Day, Halloween, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. When you've got to get a joke out there once a day, every day, you take inspiration wherever you can find it.

Halloween in particular is remarkable by its absence. In the full run of Calvin and Hobbes, there are less than a dozen Halloween-themed strips, all of which are done-in-ones. Granted, Calvin already spends a big part of the strip in fantasy scenarios and/or various costumes (i.e. his alter ego Stupendous Man), which removes some of the obvious hooks for a Halloween story. Much like adult horror fans, Calvin lives his entire life like it'll never stop being Oct. 31.

Still, there are a couple of good Halloween jokes in Calvin and Hobbes. I'm particularly fond of the strip from Oct. 31, 1995, in which Calvin's "costume" is some kind of baby-boomer terror archetype.
points: On a Halloween reread of Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes, one of its more remarkable qualities is that it usually doesn't bother with that.

articles.title: Taika Waititi Says His Star Wars Movie Is 'on Ice'
articles.summary: Director Taika Waititi has confirmed his long-in-development Star Wars movie is officially "on ice." The Thor: Ragnarok and Jojo Rabbit filmmaker provided Inverse with the update when speaking to the outlet during a press junket for his new film, Klara and the Sun.
body: "I hate to break this to you, but we're going to actually put it on ice and we're working on a different thing together," he said.

Brutal. Rumors that Disney and Lucasfilm had approached the What We Do in the Shadows filmmaker to helm a Star Wars project go as far back as January 2020. That's just a few years after he took off as the mastermind behind one of the most beloved Marvel Cinematic Universe movies to date, with an official announcement confirming he was attached to a movie arriving just a few months later.

It was mostly good news at first. In 2021, Waititi said he had finished his Star Wars movie's story, and in 2022, then-Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said the goal was to bring it to theaters in late 2023. At the time, she also admitted that Disney hadn't "locked anything in" quite yet, a fact that only became more apparent in the years that followed.

articles.title: Steam Week in Review: Steam Next Fest has over 8,000 demos, as worthless vibe coded slop levels up
articles.summary: All the interesting Steam facts for the week ending October 18.
body: We are drowning in shit. Steam Next Fest, which kicks off tomorrow, currently has 8,011 matches on its press preview landing page. That's roughly double the amount of demos featured in Steam's June 2026 Next Fest. In June 2022, Next Fest boasted just over a thousand demos.
The vast majority of these demos will be meritless slop. And I daresay many of them—though I have no way to confirm—didn't exist as concepts before October.

If you use social media, especially X, you've probably noticed an explosion of terrible clones and vibe coded mash-ups this month. You can largely thank Anthropic's new 5.5 update to its Claude Opus model for that, which offers massive efficiency gains for vibe coders. It's also been widely used to decompile commercial games and, maybe most famously, jailbreak the PS5.

It definitely feels like we've crossed a threshold this month. On October 10, the creator of Escape the Walls, an incremental punching game which itself uses AI to "increase the speed of creating the game", posted in-progress footage from the game on X.

articles.title: 23 devs teamed up to make a free game of 'innovative yet questionable volume sliders,' and it feels like browser-based WarioWare
articles.summary: Volume.art is a nice, free, cool thing on the internet, and I just think that's something worth celebrating these days. The microgame collection sees you manipulating volume sliders through various abstracted, surprising, and very funny ways.
body: It starts strong with "A man named Bow" by Alice Bottino, which kinda reminds me of the Smash Bros Home Run Contest minigame, at least as far as you're winding up to send something from the left side of the screen to the right. You drag back on the mouse to aim a bow and arrow, attempting to land it a set distance (and corresponding volume level) away.

Some of my favorite entries came from Lunacid developer Akuma Kira, like "What's This About," a riff on the criminally-maligned Elder Scrolls Oblivion persuasion pie minigame. You've got to reach a set likability level with a Gamebryo-perfect lumpy potato man, while also accounting for a game-accurate slow decay in persuasiveness as you rapidly cycle between cruelty, honesty, humor, and sucking up.

If I hadn't known about the Oblivion gag going in, it probably would have been my favorite entry⁠—"What's This About" features fairly prominently in volume.art's promo on social media. Surprise and delight is a big part of this thing, and from here there be, uh, spoilers? I guess?
points: Volume.art is a nice, free, cool thing on the internet, and I just think that's something worth celebrating these days.

articles.title: Tenebris Somnia Blends 2D Visuals With Live-Action Horror Scenes, And It’s Already On Sale At Launch
articles.summary: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension. If the player isn’t uncomfortable guiding a character through dreadful situations, well, you may as well be playing an action-adventure game (don’t mention the first Uncharted’s final act, please).
body: As the best horror games continue to push for more realistic visuals and immersive experiences, Tenebris Somnia’s twist on the genre combines old-school cool with movie-like cutscenes. It’s both jarring and original, and that’s exactly what makes for excellent horror. I want to be constantly surprised, and Tenebris Somnia makes its pixelated 2D threats even more menacing when you see live-action versions of the monsters.

Co-created by Andrés Borghi and Tobías Rusjan with Saibot Studios, and published by New Blood Interactive, the studio behind Ultrakill, Blood West, and Gloomwood, Tenebris Somnia’s style is fittingly inspired by past eras of console gaming. Its pixelated visuals make the switch to live-action cutscenes even more unsettling. It’s almost like Clock Tower, but if it randomly turned into a movie at any second. No, I’m not shaking; you are.
points: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension.

articles.title: Battlefield 6 devs to fix "Secuty" skin typo, but five-pistol outfit was intentional
articles.summary: Battlefield Studios has responded after fans accused it of using AI to generate cosmetics after spotting a "Secuty" typo on a Battlefield 6 Season 5 skin.
body: The studio acknowledged "candid feedback" from players in a statement on social media, insisting it had "hear[d] your concerns".

And though the statement did not mention AI - either to admit or deny using the generative tech - BattlefieldComm said that while the 'Secuty' typo will be addressed by a "correction update", an outfit with five pistols is intentional.

"First, let's dive into the 'Secuty' typo patches on the McNeil character," the studio wrote. "A correction update has already been planned for the Season 5 Phase 2 release. However, we recognise that letting a known visual error go live without quick acknowledgement creates confusion and erodes trust. We are reviewing how we communicate known visual bugs so you aren’t left wondering whether something was intentional or overlooked."

The five-pistol-touting Midnight Mirage skin, however, is described as an "intentional creative concept" and "a nod to over-the-top action movie tropes where an operative inexplicably has another backup weapon strapped to every spare inch of gear".
points: Battlefield Studios has responded after fans accused it of using AI to generate cosmetics after spotting a "Secuty" typo on a Battlefield 6 Season 5 skin.

articles.title: Dark Souls 2 dataminer shows off massive prototype coliseum level from early development
articles.summary: At a glance. The rough prototype looks to have been binned early in development, and it's largely avoided discussion before Doneda's work. Some portions appear to have been part of an interconnected area, others are likely different versions of the same concept.
body: Doneda, the dataminer who showed off the unused levels, has been proving a genuine authority on Dark Souls 2 in particular. Previously, they made a Nightreign-compatible version of Dark Souls 2's Eleum Loyce. Doneda has also shown off a tantalizingly ambitious early version of Dark Souls 2's The Gutter.

In hindsight, the entire pre-Sekiro Souls series (perhaps sans-Bloodborne) seems defined by difficult, rushed development cycles. Hidetaka Miyazaki took over Demon's Souls partway through as development foundered, and the final game was missing an entire archstone world. Dark Souls has its rougher, less beloved back half, particularly Lost Izalith. Dark Souls 3, though far more consistent than the prior games, had a striking world state system completely struck from it at some point.

articles.summary: Politico recently reported on a confidential draft of a proposed AI safety bill from Anthropic, the company behind Claude LLMs (via Tom's Hardware ). The bill, which has been pitched to US lawmakers, would let the government crack down on a given AI model "only if it poses a foreseeable, imminent…
body: That article pointed out similarities between these proposals and those used in California's AI legislation, and shares a quote from a spokesperson for the company. "This bill represents the proposals outlined in Anthropic’s Advanced AI Framework, which we have been advocating for with federal and state lawmakers since June," they said, calling "sensible policies we believe Congress should act on."

Just earlier this year, Anthropic's safety lead quit with a note that "the world is in peril" —and just last week, OpenAI was accused by eight US states' attorney generals of ignoring its own safety warnings for the sake of profit. Regulations like what Anthropic has proposed here arguably give tech companies the appearance of capitulation while only restricting them on their own terms. For more on AI, check out our running tally on the dumbest things tech tycoons have said so far.

videos.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – Overview Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time game launches November 5, 2026, exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2 system. Pre-orders are available now: ninten.do/6016asy0M
body: The story of Link’s adventure and growth transcends time in this classic tale, built from the ground up for Nintendo Switch 2. As you venture through the Kingdom of Hyrule, you’ll meet lively characters, battle ferocious monsters, and solve puzzles scattered throughout dungeons. Use all sorts of items, including the titular ocarina, to suit your needs and forge a path forward.

This title will support ZELDA NOTES, a game-specific service usable with the Nintendo Switch App for smart devices. Two new amiibo figures are also on the way; tap them to receive special in-game masks. And by tapping amiibo of characters from the Legend of Zelda games, you can get in-game items that may help you on your journey.
